channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Compounding Is 8th Wonder of the World, Says KKR's McVey
item.description: Henry McVey, partner, head of global macro and asset allocation and CIO of the KKR's balance sheet, joins Scarlet Fu and Tom Keene on "Bloomberg Money." They discuss private markets, asset allocation, 401K's and retirement security. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Oil Remains Primary Risk Driving Higher Rates Says Haworth
item.description: Treasuries fell as anticipation of additional Federal Reserve interest-rate hikes stoked interest in wagers on rising yields for short-maturity debt. Rob Haworth, Senior Investment Strategy Director at U.S. Bank Asset Management joins Bloomberg Businessweek Daily to discuss the markets as well as how the oil is driving rates higher. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US and China Vie For AI Lead Before Trump- Xi Summit
item.description: Less than a week before Chinese leader Xi Jinping travels to the US to meet President Donald Trump, AI has taken center stage in the bilateral relationship. In some ways the rivalry is straightforward. Most benchmarks show American models have a lead in performance that Washington very much wants to maintain, for military and economic reasons. Anja Manuel, Aspen Strategy Group Executive Director joins to discuss the upcoming meeting between the two leaders as well as what to expect from the UN General Assembly next week. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Dollar Surges to Best Week Since June on Higher Rate Outlook
item.description: The dollar staged its biggest weekly advance in more than three months after the US central bank signaled more interest-rate hikes are to come.
item.dc:creator: George Lei

item.title: KKR’s McVey Favors Private Markets as Traditional Hedges Crumble
item.description: KKR & Co.’s Henry McVey suggested the investors should shift to private markets as the traditional stock-bond diversification model breaks down under the pressure of geopolitical tensions and growing fiscal deficits.
item.dc:creator: Tom Keene and Scarlet Fu

item.title: Investors Pull $1.8 Billion From Muni Market as Return Slump Extends
item.description: Investors pulled about $1.8 billion out of the municipal bond market this week with returns for state and local government debt on track to tumble for the third consecutive month.
item.dc:creator: Aashna Shah

item.title: Earnings, Not the Fed, Are Driving Stocks: UBS's Lovell
item.description: Nadia Lovell, head of global equity strategy at UBS Global Wealth Management, says strong earnings and broadening profit growth should keep stocks moving higher even as rising rates create near-term volatility. “What’s gonna drive this market is earnings. It’s not valuation expansion,” Lovell says on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Odd Lots: How Beer Distributors and Other “Little Guys” Got Rich
item.description:
America's “Main Street Millionaires” comprise about three million private business owners who have amassed one of the country's most concentrated pools of wealth. That's according to a study conducted by Owen Zidar and Eric Zwick.
On this episode of the Odd Lots podcast, economists and authors of The Everywhere Millionaire: Who Is Really Rich in America and How They Got There, tell Tracy Alloway and Joe Weisenthal how "little guys" like beverage distributors, dentists and car wash owners have become millionaires hiding in plain sight. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Investor Sentiment Plunges to 16-Month Low, AAII Survey Shows
item.description: Investor sentiment fell to its lowest point since 2025, a weekly survey from the American Association of Individual Investors showed, as oil prices remained elevated while the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023.
item.dc:creator: Geoffrey Morgan

item.title: College Students Look for Leg Up to Get Wall Street Job
item.description: Bloomberg Finance Editor Daniel Taub talks about the lengths college students are going to as they try to land a lucrative job on Wall Street. He speaks on "Bloomberg Money." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: 'Hike Doesn't Change Fundamentals,' says Cetera's Goldman
item.description: Gene Goldman, CIO of Cetera, reacts to the inflation expectations and overall market volatility following the Fed's rate decision by telling Bloomberg's Paul Sweeney and Scarlet Fu that it's one and done (maybe two and done), not the start of something bigger. It's insurance against sticky inflation, not a return to aggressive tightening. Markets had priced in too much. Federal Reserve officials failed to adequately respond to repeated warnings about the deteriorating financial condition of Silicon Valley Bank before its 2023 failure, a new draft report found, according to Fed Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman and other people familiar with the document. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Stocks Waver as Treasuries Yield Resume Advance
item.description: Jonathan Ferro, Lisa Abramowicz and Annmarie Hordern speak daily with leaders and decision makers from Wall Street to Washington and beyond. No other program better positions investors and executives for the trading day than "Bloomberg Surveillance." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Yen Pares BOJ-Fueled Declines as Nikkei Reports a Rate Check
item.description: The yen pared declines on Friday, with the Nikkei newspaper reporting that the Bank of Japan inquired with market participants about exchange-rate levels, a step often seen as a precursor to official intervention.
item.dc:creator: Sydney Maki, John Cheng and Cameron Fozi

item.title: Specialty Insurer Orion180 Falls 2.8% After $240 Million IPO
item.description: Orion180 Insurance Group Inc. fell 2.8% in its first day of trading after the company raised $240 million from its initial public offering.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Hughes

item.title: VW Cuts Outlook After Writedown on Porsche, Decline in China
item.description: Volkswagen AG slashed its profit forecast after a sharp contraction in China and a €6 billion ($6.9 billion) writedown tied to sports-car maker Porsche AG, deepening concerns about the strains facing the global auto industry.
item.dc:creator: William Wilkes

item.title: Screwworm Reappears in New Mexico Ahead of Port Reopening
item.description: The New World screwworm resurfaced in New Mexico just as a major gateway for Mexican cattle imports is poised to open in the state.
item.dc:creator: Ilena Peng

item.title: Saudis Give European Oil Buyers No Supplies for Next Month
item.description: Saudi Aramco told at least two oil refining customers in Europe that they will be allocated no crude next month under long-term agreements after the kingdom’s key pipeline to the Red Sea was attacked, people informed of the decision said.
item.dc:creator: Sherry Su

item.title: Copper Notches 11th Weekly Gain in Twelve on Chinese Buying
item.description: Copper notched its 11th weekly gain in twelve as signs of a rebound in Chinese demand helped to offset hawkish messaging from the Federal Reserve about the likelihood of more interest-rate rises.
item.dc:creator: Eddie Spence

item.title: S&P 500 Volume Spikes on $7 Trillion Options Day: Markets Wrap
item.description: The last stretch of a busy week for markets saw stocks churning as bond yields rose, with investors also facing the expiration of a pile of options that spurred a surge in trading volume.
item.dc:creator: Rita Nazareth

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for Sept. 18
item.description: Oil fell for a third straight session amid shifting concerns about Middle East supply, with Saudi Arabia pausing some sales to Europe though traders and analysts saying buffers still hold for now.
item.dc:creator: Kanoko Matsuyama and Mia Gindis
